summary: Remote-controlled shell backdoor over WebSocket in tsihealth-client
details: The package's exported `provider()` function opens a WebSocket to a configured server at `<server>/ws/<id>` and, on each incoming JSON message of type `cmd`, writes the command string into a spawned `/bin/bash --norc --noprofile` process (or `cmd.exe` with `windowsHide:true` on Windows) via `shell.stdin.write(command+"\r\n")`, streaming stdout and stderr back over the socket. This gives whoever operates the configured server full interactive shell execution on any host that runs `provider()`. The single-file main (`index.js`, ~129 KB on two lines) is obfuscated with a hand-rolled VM-bytecode interpreter (base64-encoded opcode arrays, `_0xXXXXXX` identifier names) and carries a header comment discouraging inspection ("Please do not crack or read this; respect the author of this library."), hiding the backdoor logic from casual review. The package is presented as a health-monitoring client, a purpose that does not require piping network-supplied bytes into an OS shell.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
